question: Are employers permitted to lower anyone's pay in order to comply with gender wage equality rules?
answer: No, an employer is explicitly prohibited from reducing the wage rate of any employee for the purpose of complying with gender non-discrimination requirements.
quote:
No employer shall,—
(i) for the purposes of complying with the provisions of sub-section (1), reduce the rate of wages of any employee;

question: Can I pay my worker a bit less than the government's set minimum wage if they agree to it?
answer: No, an employer is legally prohibited from paying any employee less than the minimum wage rate that has been officially notified by the appropriate government.
quote: No employer shall pay to any employee wages less than the minimum rate of wages notified by the appropriate Government.

question: What factors must the Central Government consider when determining the floor wage?
answer: The Central Government is required to determine the floor wage by considering the minimum living standards of a worker in the prescribed manner.
quote: The Central Government shall fix floor wage taking into account minimum living standards of a worker in such manner as may be prescribed

question: I have to work on my weekly rest day. Will I get extra pay for that?
answer: The Code on Wages lets the appropriate Government provide for payment for work on a day of rest at a rate not less than the overtime rate, so you are entitled to it where the government has provided for it.
quote: provide for payment for work on a day of rest at a rate not less than the overtime rate.
ai_note: Edited answer: the section is a power of the government ('may provide'), not a direct right.

question: Can the government require certain establishments to pay employee wages strictly through bank transfers or cheques?
answer: Yes, the appropriate Government has the authority to issue a notification specifying certain industrial or other establishments where employers are mandated to pay wages exclusively by cheque or through bank account credit.
quote: Provided that the appropriate Government may, by notification, specify the industrial or other establishment, the employer of which shall pay to every person employed in such industrial or other establishment, the wages only by cheque or by crediting the wages in his bank account.

question: I just quit my job last week—when does my former boss legally have to clear my final paycheck?
answer: When an employee is removed, dismissed, retrenched, has resigned, or becomes unemployed due to the closure of the establishment, their final wages must be paid within two working days of that event.
quotes: removed or dismissed from service

retrenched or has resigned from service, or became unemployed due to closure of the establishment, the wages payable to him shall be paid within two working days of his removal, dismissal, retrenchment or, as the case may be, his resignation.
revision_note: Added the closure-of-establishment wording to the quotes.

question: What is the maximum percentage of an employee's wages that can be deducted in any single wage period?
answer: The total amount of authorized deductions made from an employee's wages in any wage period is capped at fifty percent.
quote: the total amount of deductions which may be made under sub-section (2) in any wage period from the wages of an employee shall not exceed fifty per cent. of such wages.

question: If a bunch of us workers suddenly go on a wildcat strike without giving proper notice, how much extra can the boss cut from our pay?
answer: If ten or more workers act together to stay away from work without a valid reason and without giving required notice, the employer can deduct an extra amount not exceeding eight days of wages in lieu of that notice.
quote: if ten or more employed persons acting in concert absent themselves without due notice (that is to say without giving the notice which is required under the terms of their contracts of employment) and without reasonable cause, such deduction from any such person may include such amount not exceeding his wages for eight days as may by any such terms be due to the employer in lieu of due notice.

question: What is the minimum number of days an employee must work in an accounting year to be eligible for an annual minimum bonus?
answer: An employee must complete at least thirty days of work in an accounting year to qualify for the annual minimum bonus.
quote: who has put in at least thirty days work in an accounting year, an annual minimum bonus calculated at the rate of eight and one-third per cent.

question: If I get fired for fighting with someone at work, can my boss refuse to pay my bonus?
answer: Yes, an employee is disqualified from receiving a bonus if they are dismissed from service for riotous or violent behavior on the company's premises.
quote:
an employee shall be disqualified from receiving bonus under this Code, if he is dismissed from service for––
(a) fraud; or
(b) riotous or violent behaviour while on the premises of the establishment

question: What is the standard time limit for an employer to credit an employee's bonus into their bank account after the accounting year ends?
answer: Within eight months from the close of the accounting year, by crediting the bonus to the employee's bank account. On the employer's application and for sufficient reasons, the appropriate Government can extend this period, but the total extension cannot exceed two years.
ai_note: Checked: the 2-year maximum extension is in the full section text.
quotes: All amounts payable to an employee by way of bonus under this Code shall be paid by crediting it in the bank account of the employee by his employer within a period of eight months from the close of the accounting year

upon an application made to it by the employer and for sufficient reasons, by order, extend the said period of eight months to such further period or periods as it thinks fit; so, however, that the total period so extended shall not in any case exceed two years
revision_note: Added the extension proviso as a quote.

question: My boss hasn't paid me what I'm owed, and it's been more than three years since the issue started. Can I still file an application to get my money?
answer: Possibly. A claim application should normally be filed within three years from the date the claim arose. After three years, the authority may still entertain it, but only if you show sufficient cause for the delay.
quotes: may be filed within a period of three years from the date on which claims referred to in sub-section (1) arises
may, entertain the application after three years on sufficient cause being shown by the applicant for such delay
revision_note: Answer made conditional on showing sufficient cause; added the three-year limit quote.

question: What is the maximum number of members allowed on the Grievance Redressal Committee?
answer: The total number of members on the Grievance Redressal Committee cannot exceed ten individuals.
quote: The total number of members of the Grievance Redressal Committee shall not exceed ten

question: A strike is already going on at our workplace. Do the workers still have to give a separate strike notice, and does the employer have to inform anyone?
answer: No separate strike or lock-out notice is needed when a strike or lock-out is already in existence. But the employer must send intimation of the strike or lock-out, on the day it is declared, to the authority specified by the appropriate Government.
quotes: The notice of strike or lock-out under this section shall not be necessary where there is already in existence a strike or, as the case may be, lock-out, but the employer shall send intimation of such lock-out or strike on the day on which it is declared, to such authority as may be specified by the appropriate Government
revision_note: Question rephrased: a strike already exists (no 'planning a future strike').

question: What is the compensation amount a qualified laid-off worker is entitled to receive from their employer?
answer: A qualified worker who is laid-off must be paid compensation equal to fifty per cent of the total basic wages and dearness allowance that would have been payable had they not been laid-off, excluding intervening weekly holidays.
ai_note: Audit #47: added the quote for the weekly-holiday exclusion.
quotes: compensation which shall be equal to fifty per cent. of the total of the basic wages and dearness allowance that would have been payable to him, had he not been so laid-off
except for such weekly holidays as may intervene

question: I've been working at a factory for over a year now, and my boss is planning to retrench me (end my job permanently). What notice and pay am I supposed to get before I go?
answer: If you have at least one year of continuous service, the employer must (a) give you one month's written notice stating the reasons, or pay wages for the notice period instead; (b) pay retrenchment compensation of fifteen days' average pay (or such other days as the appropriate Government notifies) for every completed year of continuous service or part of a year over six months; and (c) serve notice on the appropriate Government or the authority it specifies.
ai_note: Audit #48: added quotes for retrenchment compensation and notice to the Government.
quotes: who has been in continuous service for not less than one year under an employer shall be retrenched by that employer until

(a) the worker has been given one month's notice in writing indicating the reasons for retrenchment and the period of notice has expired, or the worker has been paid in lieu of such notice, wages for the period of the notice;

compensation which shall be equivalent to fifteen days' average pay, or average pay of such days as may be notified by the appropriate Government, for every completed year of continuous service or any part thereof in excess of six months
notice in such manner as may be prescribed is served on the appropriate Government or such authority as may be specified by the appropriate Government by notification
revision_note: Quotes now cover the one-year condition and the per-year compensation rule.

question: How should an employer determine which worker to retrench when there is no prior agreement?
answer: In the absence of an agreement between the employer and the worker, the employer must ordinarily retrench the person who was most recently employed in that specific category of workers, unless there are recorded reasons to do otherwise.
quote: in the absence of any agreement between the employer and the worker in this behalf, the employer shall ordinarily retrench the worker who was the last person to be employed in that category, unless for reasons to be recorded the employer retrenches any other worker.

question: I was retrenched from my job a few months ago, but now my old boss is hiring again. Do I get first choice to go back to work there?
answer: Yes. If the employer proposes to employ anyone within one year of the retrenchment, retrenched workers who are citizens of India must be given an opportunity to offer themselves for re-employment, and those who do get preference over other persons.
ai_note: Audit #50: answer now says 'retrenched' (not 'laid-off'); added the preference quote.
quotes: Where any worker is retrenched and the employer proposes to take into his employment any person within one year of such retrenchment, he shall, in such manner as may be prescribed, give an opportunity to the retrenched workers who are citizens of India to offer themselves for re-employment and such retrenched workers who offer themselves for re-employment shall have preference over other persons.
shall have preference over other persons

question: How many days in advance must an employer give notice before closing down an undertaking, and which types of establishments are exempt from this requirement?
answer: An employer must provide at least sixty days' notice to the appropriate Government before closing an undertaking, clearly stating the reasons for the closure. However, this requirement does not apply to establishments that employed fewer than fifty workers on any day in the preceding twelve months, or to those set up for construction projects like buildings, bridges, roads, canals, or dams.
quote:
An employer who intends to close down an undertaking shall serve, at least sixty days before the date on which the intended closure is to become effective, a notice, in such manner as may be prescribed, on the appropriate Government stating clearly the reasons for the intended closure of the undertaking:
Provided that nothing in this section shall apply to—
(i) an industrial establishment in which less than fifty workers are employed or were employed on any day in the preceding twelve months;
(ii) an industrial establishment set up for the construction of buildings, bridges, roads, canals, dams or for other construction work or project.
ai_note: Checked: the exemptions (<50 workers, construction) are in the full section text.

question: I might have to retrench a few workers soon. Do I need to pay anything extra into a special fund for them, and if so, how much?
answer: Yes. For every retrenched worker, the employer contributes to the worker re-skilling fund an amount equal to fifteen days' wages last drawn by the worker (or such other number of days as the Central Government notifies).
quote: the contribution of the employer of an industrial establishment an amount equal to fifteen days wages last drawn by the worker immediately before the retrenchment, or such other number of days as may be notified by the Central Government, for every retrenched worker in case of retrenchment only;
ai_note: Edited question: 'lay off' -> 'retrench' (the re-skilling fund applies to retrenchment).
revision_note: Added the 'or such other number of days as notified' qualification.

question: Who receives the gratuity if an employee passes away, and how is the share handled if that recipient is a minor?
answer: In the event of an employee's death, the gratuity is paid to their nominee or, if no nomination exists, to their legal heirs. If any nominee or heir is a minor, their share must be deposited with the notified competent authority, who will invest it in a prescribed bank or financial institution for the minor's benefit until they reach majority.
quote: in the case of death of the employee, gratuity payable to him shall be paid to his nominee or, if no nomination has been made, to his heirs, and where any such nominees or heirs is a minor, the share of such minor, shall be deposited with the competent authority as may be notified by the appropriate Government who shall invest the same for the benefit of such minor in such bank or other financial institution, as may be prescribed by the appropriate Government, until such minor attains majority.

question: I've been working here for over a year now and want to update my gratuity nomination to include my spouse instead of my brother. Can I change who gets my gratuity after I've already named someone?
answer: Yes. You can modify your nomination at any time by giving your employer written intimation, in the prescribed form, of your intention to do so. The change must follow the family rules: if you have a family, the nomination must be in favour of one or more family members (a nomination of a non-family member is void), and a nomination made when you had no family becomes invalid once you acquire a family, after which you must make a fresh nomination in favour of family members.
quotes: A nomination may, subject to the provisions of sub-sections (3) and (4), be modified by an employee at any time, after giving to his employer a written intimation in such form and in such manner as may be prescribed by the appropriate Government, of his intention to do so.

If an employee has a family at the time of making a nomination, the nomination shall be made in favour of one or more members of his family, and any nomination made by such employee in favour of a person who is not a member of his family shall be void.

if the employee subsequently acquires a family, such nomination shall forthwith become invalid and the employee shall make, within such time as may be prescribed by the appropriate Government, a fresh nomination in favour of one or more members of his family
revision_note: Added sub-sections (3) and (4) on family nominations.

question: What should an employer do if there is a dispute regarding the amount of gratuity payable or who is entitled to receive it?
answer: If a dispute arises regarding the gratuity amount, its admissibility, or the rightful recipient, the employer must deposit the amount they admit is payable with the competent authority.
quote: the employer shall deposit with the competent authority such amount as he admits to be payable by him as gratuity.

question: I run a small shop with a dozen workers—do I need to buy insurance for paying out gratuity, or can I skip it if I set up a special fund instead?
answer: From the date notified by the appropriate Government, every employer (other than government establishments) must insure its gratuity liability with a regulated insurance company. The government may exempt employers who already have an approved gratuity fund, or who employ five hundred or more persons and set one up.
ai_note: Edited answer: added that the duty starts from a notified date and excludes government employers.
quotes: With effect from such date as may be notified by the appropriate Government in this behalf, every employer, other than an employer or an establishment belonging to, or under the control of, the Central Government or a State Government, shall, subject to the provisions of sub-section (2), obtain an insurance in the manner prescribed by the Central Government, for his liability for payment towards the gratuity under this Chapter, from any insurance company regulated by the Authority

exempt any employer who had already established an approved gratuity fund in respect of his employees and who desires to continue such arrangement, and every employer employing five hundred or more persons who establishes an approved gratuity fund
revision_note: Added the main insurance obligation (date, government exception) as a quote.

question: Are there any restrictions on a pregnant woman performing strenuous or physically demanding work before her expected delivery?
answer: Yes, a pregnant woman cannot be required by her employer to perform arduous work, long hours of standing, or any work likely to adversely affect her health or pregnancy during the specified period prior to her expected delivery, provided she makes a request to that effect.
quote: no pregnant woman shall, on a request being made by her in this behalf, be required by her employer to do, during the period specified in sub-section (4), any work which is of an arduous nature or which involves long hours of standing or which in any way is likely to interfere with her pregnancy

question: I'm expecting my third child soon and am wondering how many weeks of maternity leave I'm allowed to take?
answer: If you already have two or more surviving children, you are entitled to a maximum maternity benefit period of twelve weeks, with no more than six weeks coming before your expected delivery date.
quote: the maximum period entitled to maternity benefit by a woman having two or more surviving children shall be twelve weeks of which not more than six weeks shall precede the date of her expected delivery

question: What is the monetary amount of the medical bonus a female employee is entitled to receive if her employer does not provide free pre-natal and post-natal care?
answer: An eligible woman is entitled to a medical bonus of three thousand five hundred rupees, or an amount notified by the Central Government, if free pre-natal confinement and post-natal care are not provided by the employer.
quote: be entitled to receive from her employer a medical bonus of three thousand five hundred rupees or such amount as may be notified by the Central Government, if no pre-natal confinement and post-natal care is provided for by the employer free of charge.

question: I recently had a tubectomy operation and need to take time off work to recover. Am I entitled to paid leave for this, and if so, for how long?
answer: Yes, if you undergo a tubectomy operation, you are entitled to two weeks of paid leave at the maternity benefit rate immediately following the procedure, provided you show the required proof.
quote: In case of tubectomy operation, a woman shall, on production of such proof as may be prescribed by the Central Government, be entitled to leave with wages at the rate of maternity benefit for a period of two weeks immediately following the day of her tubectomy operation.

question: How many times a day is a female employee permitted to visit the crèche facility?
answer: An employer must permit a female employee to visit the crèche four times a day, which includes her allowed rest intervals.
quote: Provided that the employer shall allow four visits a day to the crèche by the woman, which shall also include the intervals of rest allowed to her:

question: I deliver food through a delivery app and want to get registered under the new rules. How old do I need to be, and what do I need to submit to get my registration number?
answer: To get registered as a gig or platform worker, you must be at least sixteen years of age (or another age prescribed by the Central Government) and submit a self-declaration along with an application form and documents including your Aadhaar number. Once you apply, you will be assigned a distinguishable number.
ai_note: Checked: Aadhaar and the distinguishable number are in the full section text.

question: What are the funding sources that can be used for the social security schemes established for gig workers and platform workers?
answer: Social security schemes for gig workers and platform workers can be funded through various sources, including being wholly or partly funded by the Central and State Governments, through contributions from aggregators or beneficiaries, from corporate social responsibility funds, or from any other specified source.
quote:
Any scheme notified by the Central Government under sub-section (1), may be—
(a) wholly funded by the Central Government; or
(b) partly funded by the Central Government and partly funded by the State Government; or
(c) wholly funded by the contributions of the aggregators; or
(d) partly funded by the Central Government, partly funded by the State Government and partly funded through contributions collected from the beneficiaries of the scheme or the aggregators, as may be specified in the scheme framed by the Central Government; or
(e) funded from corporate social responsibility fund within the meaning of Companies Act, 2013; or
(f) any other source.

question: Can my boss cut my pay or take away my benefits just because they now have to pay contributions under the new social security rules?
answer: No, an employer cannot reduce your wages or total benefits simply because they are required to pay contributions under the Code.
ai_note: Audit #64: the section does cover total benefits, not just wages; added that quote.
quotes: No employer in relation to an establishment to which this Code or any scheme framed thereunder applies shall, by reason only of his liability for the payment of any contribution under this Code, or any charges thereunder reduce whether directly or indirectly, the wages of any employee
or the total quantum of benefits to which such employee is entitled under the terms of his employment

question: Am I required to pay for any medical examinations or safety measures provided by my employer to detect occupational diseases?
answer: No, employers are prohibited from charging employees for anything provided for workplace safety and health, including medical examinations and investigations to detect occupational diseases.
quote: ensure that no charge is levied on any employee, in respect of anything done or provided for maintenance of safety and health at workplace including conduct of medical examination and investigation for the purpose of detecting occupational diseases

question: I work as a journalist—how many hours am I allowed to work over a four-week stretch according to the rules?
answer: A working journalist's hours of work are subject to a maximum of 144 hours during any period of four consecutive weeks.
quote: the hours of work for working journalist shall, subject to a maximum of one hundred and forty-four hours of work during any period of four consecutive weeks

question: When must an employee be given compensatory holidays if they miss their scheduled weekly rest days due to an official exemption?
answer: A worker who loses weekly holidays due to an exemption order must be provided with an equal number of compensatory holidays either within the same month they were due or during the following two months.
quote: the worker shall be allowed, within the month in which the holidays were due or within the two months immediately following that month, compensatory holidays of equal number to the holidays, so deprived.

question: I work night shifts that go past midnight. How does the law count my weekly holiday and my workdays when my shift bleeds into the next morning?
answer: For workers on shifts extending past midnight, your weekly holiday of a whole day is counted as a 24-hour period starting right when your night shift ends. Similarly, your next day is considered to start when that shift ends, and any hours you worked after midnight are counted as part of the previous day.
quote:
a weekly holiday for a whole day shall mean in his case a period of twenty-four consecutive hours beginning when his shift ends;
(b) the following day for him shall be deemed to be the period of twenty-four hours beginning when such shift ends, and the hours he has worked after midnight shall be counted in the previous day.

question: How many days of unused annual leave can a worker carry forward to the next calendar year under standard conditions?
answer: Under standard conditions, the total number of days of unused leave that a worker can carry forward to the succeeding calendar year is capped at thirty days. However, any leave that the worker applied for but was refused can be carried forward without any limit.
quote: the total number of days of leave that may be carried forward to a succeeding year shall not exceed thirty days; and (b) such worker, who has applied for leave with wages but has not been given such leave in accordance with this sub-section and the rules made thereunder shall be entitled to carry forward the leave refused without any limit

question: I run a small unit and want to know if I can have female staff work early in the morning before 6 or late in the evening after 7, and what I need to keep in mind?
answer: Yes, women can work before 6 a.m. and after 7 p.m. provided they give their consent and the employer follows prescribed conditions regarding safety, holidays, and working hours.
quote: they may also be employed, with their consent before 6 a.m. and beyond 7 p.m. subject to such conditions relating to safety, holidays and working hours or any other condition to be observed by the employer as may be prescribed by the appropriate Government.

question: What measures must an employer take if the government determines that certain operations are hazardous for female workers?
answer: When the appropriate Government decides that employing women in certain operations or establishments is hazardous to their health and safety, it can mandate that the employer provide proper safeguards before women are allowed to work on those operations.
quote: such Government may in the prescribed manner, require the employer to provide adequate safeguards prior to the employment of women for such operation.

question: I pay my staff weekly instead of every day—how many hours are they allowed to work in a week so we don't cross the limit?
answer: For employees whose wage period is not daily, their normal working hours must be arranged so that their total weekly hours do not exceed forty-eight hours.
quote: The number of hours of work which shall constitute a normal working day for an employee whose wage period is other than on a daily basis shall be so fixed that the total number of weekly working hours shall not exceed forty-eight hours.

question: How are employees informed about their designated weekly rest day or any changes to it?
answer: Employees are informed of their designated rest day or any subsequent changes by a notice displayed at a conspicuous place in the workplace or through electronic means before the change takes effect.
quote: the employee shall be informed of the day fixed as the rest day and of any subsequent change in the rest day before the change is effected, by display of a notice to that effect at a conspicuous place in the place of employment or electronically.

question: Hey, as a worker, am I supposed to get some kind of wage slip when I'm paid, and can my boss send it to me online?
answer: Yes. Your employer must issue a wage slip, electronically or in physical form, on or before the payment of wages.
ai_note: Audit #74: answer now says 'on or before payment of wages'.
quotes: Every employer shall issue wage slips, electronically or in physical form to the employees in Form V under sub-section (3) of section 50 on or before payment of wages.

question: What methods are legally permitted for making the actual payment of gratuity to an eligible employee, nominee, or legal heir?
answer: The gratuity payment must be disbursed either through a Demand Draft or by directly crediting the amount into the bank account of the eligible person.
quote: The gratuity payable under the Code shall be paid through Demand Draft or by crediting in the bank account of the eligible employee, nominee or legal heir, as the case may be.

question: My wife just had a baby and we need to claim her maternity benefit, but I'm worried because I didn't use the exact official form. Will her claim get rejected just because we didn't use the specified form?
answer: No, a claim will not be considered invalid simply because the application was not presented in the specified form.
quote: Provided further that no claim shall be invalid merely because the claimant failed to present her application in specified form.

question: What is the minimum age requirement for an unorganised worker, gig worker, or platform worker to be registered on the designated Central Government portal?
answer: An unorganised worker, gig worker, or platform worker must have completed sixteen years of age to be required to register on the designated portal of the Central Government.
quotes: Every unorganised worker, who has completed sixteen years of age shall be required to be registered under section 113, on the designated Portal of the Central Government.
Every gig and platform worker, who has completed sixteen years of age shall be required to be registered
revision_note: Added rule 48(2)(a) for gig and platform workers.

question: I run a small factory with about 65 workers on site, and a few employees have been asking about daycare. Do I actually have to set up a crèche for their kids, and is there any way we can share one with nearby businesses to save costs?
answer: Yes, if you ordinarily employ more than fifty workers, you must ensure that a crèche facility is provided and maintained for employees' children under six. Establishments are also permitted to pool their resources or avail themselves of a common crèche facility provided by governments, municipalities, private entities, NGOs, or other organizations.
ai_note: Fixed quote: the draft quote skipped text in the middle; now one continuous verbatim span.
quotes: wherein more than fifty workers are ordinarily employed, a crèche facility is provided and maintained for the use of children under the age of six years of employees

an establishment can avail common crèche facility of the Central Government, State Government, municipality or private entity or provided by non-governmental organisation or by any other organisation or group of establishments may pool their resources for setting up of common crèche

question: What is the maximum number of hours a worker is permitted to work in an establishment during a week?
answer: A worker cannot be required or permitted to work for more than forty-eight hours in a single week within an establishment.
quote: No worker shall be required or allowed to work in an establishment for more than forty eight hours in a week.

question: If we workers decide to go on strike at our factory, who do we actually need to hand the notice over to?
answer: The strike notice must be given directly to the employer of the industrial establishment. A copy of this notice also needs to be sent electronically or by speed post to the concerned conciliation officer, the Chief Labour Commissioner (Central), and the Secretary of the Ministry of Labour and Employment.
quote: given in Form-XI, to the employer of an industrial establishment , which shall be duly signed by the Secretary of the concerned registered Trade Union or where there is no registered Trade Union, by five elected representatives of the workers giving the notice relating to the concerned industrial establishment, endorsing the copy thereof electronically or by speed post to the concerned conciliation officer, Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) and the Secretary, Ministry of Labour and Employment.

question: Who must be notified when an employer decides to retrench a worker with at least one year of continuous service?
answer: When an employer retrenches a worker who has completed at least one year of continuous service, prior notice in the specified form must be served to the Central Government and the concerned Deputy Chief Labour Commissioner (Central).
quotes: If an employer desires to retrench any worker employed in his industrial establishment who has been in continuous service for not less than one year, such employer shall serve prior notice of retrenchment in Form-XIII to the Central Government and to the concerned Deputy Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) through e-mail or speed post
revision_note: Quote now includes the one-year continuous-service condition.

question: I had to let a worker go recently—how soon do I need to send their fifteen days' wages to the re-skilling fund, and how do I do it?
answer: As an employer, you must electronically transfer an amount equal to fifteen days of the worker's last drawn wages into the designated fund within ten days of the retrenchment.
quote: Every employer who has retrenched a worker in industrial establishment, shall, within ten days from the date of such retrenchment, electronically transfer an amount equivalent to fifteen days of last drawn wages of such retrenched worker or workers in the fund

question: What is the timeline and designated form for an eligible employee to apply for gratuity to their employer?
answer: An eligible employee should ordinarily apply for gratuity to their employer in Form-IV within a period of thirty days from the date the gratuity became payable.
quote: An employee who is eligible for payment of gratuity under the Code, or any person authorised, in writing, to act on his behalf, shall apply, ordinarily within a period of thirty days from the date the gratuity became payable, in Form-IV to the employer

question: If an employee agrees to work overtime, how must the overtime work period be calculated, and at what minimum rate should they be compensated for those extra hours?
answer: The period of overtime work is calculated on a daily or weekly basis, whichever is more favourable to the worker, and the employer must pay for overtime work at a rate of not less than twice the normal rate of wages.
ai_note: Audit #84: added the OSH Code quote for daily/weekly calculation.
quotes: at the overtime rate which shall not be less than twice the normal rate of wages.
the period of overtime work shall be calculated on a daily basis or weekly basis, whichever is more favourable to such worker

question: How many hours make up a normal working day for an employee whose wage period is daily?
answer: Eight hours. The rules prescribe eight hours as the normal working day for an employee whose wage period is daily.
ai_note: Audit 2 (#13): answer limited to the normal working day; dropped the 'maximum' claim.
quotes: The number of hours of work which shall constitute normal working day for an employee whose wage period is on a daily basis shall be eight hours

question: If an employer provides the worker with a one-month written notice for retrenchment, within how many days must the corresponding notice be served to the Central Government and the Deputy Chief Labour Commissioner?
answer: When an employer gives prior written notice to a worker, the corresponding notice of retrenchment must be served to the Central Government and the concerned Deputy Chief Labour Commissioner within three days from the date the notice was served on the worker.
quote: where prior notice is given to a worker under clause (a) of section 70 of the Code, notice of such retrenchment shall be served within three days from the date on which such notice is served on the worker

question: If an industrial establishment has no registered trade union, who must sign the strike notice, and to which specific authorities must a copy of this notice be endorsed?
answer: When there is no registered trade union, the strike notice must be signed by five elected representatives of the workers. A copy of this notice must be endorsed electronically or by speed post to the concerned conciliation officer, Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) and the Secretary, Ministry of Labour and Employment.
quote: where there is no registered Trade Union, by five elected representatives of the workers giving the notice relating to the concerned industrial establishment, endorsing the copy thereof electronically or by speed post to the concerned conciliation officer, Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) and the Secretary, Ministry of Labour and Employment.

question: What is the specific monetary amount of the medical bonus that a female employee is entitled to receive from her employer if she qualifies for maternity benefit and no free pre-natal or post-natal care is provided?

question: How many daily visits is a female employee permitted to make to the workplace crèche, and what specific information must she receive in writing and electronically regarding her benefits upon joining the establishment?

question: Within what time frame must an aggregator share the details of existing gig and platform workers on the designated portal from the commencement of the rules, and what minimum age requirement must those workers meet to be eligible for registration?

question: If an eligible worker is laid off, under what circumstances can the employer deny paying them any lay-off compensation?
answer: No compensation is payable after the first forty-five days of lay-off in a twelve-month period if the worker and employer have agreed to that. Compensation is also not payable if the worker refuses alternative employment offered at the wages he would normally have been paid, in the same establishment or another establishment of the same employer in the same town or village or within eight kilometres, where in the employer's opinion it needs no special skill or previous experience and he can do it; if he does not present himself for work at the appointed time during normal working hours at least once a day; or if the lay-off is due to a strike or slowing-down of production by workers in another part of the establishment.

question: If multiple employees suddenly go on strike without giving the required notice and without reasonable cause, what is the maximum amount that can be deducted from each of their wages in lieu of that notice?

question: If I hire someone on a written contract for a set period, does that count as fixed term employment, and do they get the same benefits as my permanent staff?

question: I do some work from home and also take on casual jobs — do I count as an unorganised worker?

question: I hire workers through a middleman for my business operations—do these workers count as contract labour, and are there any exceptions if someone is hired regularly?
